Show the summary of a saved run. It says how often each assistant mentions you and your competitors, and which sites the answers cite. Without a run id it shows the newest run. The numbers are worked out again from the saved answers with the brand and competitors in llmention.yaml, so you can still compare old runs after you edit the file. --html writes a single page you can share.

Related commands:
  llmention run
  llmention history list

Output:
  Shows text you can read in your terminal.
  Use --json to get JSON for scripts and other programs.
  Use --jq to filter the JSON output with a jq expression.
  Use --template to format the output with a Go template.

Usage:
  llmention report [run-id] [run-id] [flags]

Examples:
llmention report
llmention report --answers
llmention report --diff
llmention report --trend
llmention report --html report.html
llmention report --format markdown >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
llmention report 20261026-1608 --details
llmention report --fail-under mention-rate=30%

Flags:
      --answers                  Print every answer instead of the summary
      --details                  Print every metric of the run
      --diff                     Compare with the run before it, or compare two run ids
      --fail-under stringArray   Fail with exit code 7 when a number is below a threshold, for example mention-rate=40% (repeatable)
      --format string            Summary format: text or markdown (default "text")
  -h, --help                     help for report
      --html string              Write the report as one HTML file to this path
      --runs int                 How many recent runs --trend and --html include (default 12)
      --suite string             Only look at runs of this suite (default: your prompts)
      --trend                    Show your mention rate across recent runs

Global Flags:
      --config string     Path to the config file
      --dry-run           Preview changes without performing them
      --include-meta      Wrap machine output as {data, meta} (commands that expose request metadata)
      --jq string         Transform stable JSON output with a jq expression (commands with machine output)
      --json              Output stable JSON instead of the human view
      --no-ansi           Disable all ANSI/control sequences in human output
      --no-color          Disable color in human output
      --no-pager          Never use a pager for long human output
      --no-prompt         Never block on an interactive prompt
      --plain             Print unstyled, copy-safe text (commands with human output)
      --quiet             Suppress non-essential output
      --template string   Render stable JSON output through a Go text/template (commands with machine output)
